clue.text: Get in touch with one during voyage going west, then east

indicators.note: the one letter sits during, that is in the middle of, the voyage word
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the voyage word turns round

parts.note: to sail is to voyage
the Roman numeral for one is I
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A traveller makes contact with someone on a ship that sails west and then east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns SAIL into LIAS; 'during' puts I inside it to make LIAIS, and E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to keep up contact and cooperate with another party, a synonym for getting in touch.

clue.text: Period of being especially entertained by fantastic final

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within the host's house, so one piece goes inside the other
something fantastic is wild and unreal, a signal that the letters of final are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a stretch of time when they were thrilled by a terrific last match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' signals an anagram of the five letters of 'final'; 'entertained by' sets the abbreviation inside that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifespan is the whole duration of a creature's existence, its time of being alive.

clue.text: Company, very advanced, rising above trouble to supply fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece above another comes first
in a down clue, rising means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards, reversing them

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation of advanced, as in A level
ado is fuss or trouble, as in much ado

explanation.surface: A firm with a very forward outlook rises above its difficulties to sell produce.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the three abbreviations upwards, and 'above' puts them over the word for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocado is the pear-shaped green-skinned fruit of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Exercise in singing unaccompanied stopped of bygone era

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Exercise in singing unaccompanied stopped of bygone era', is garbled: its tail repeats 18-across and no wordplay for the letters inside SOLO (FEGGI) survives.
annotationWithheld.clue: Exercise in singing unaccompanied stopped of bygone era

clue.text: In role of investigator harangue candidate

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in acting as chairman
a PI is a private investigator, a detective
to rant is to harangue loudly

explanation.surface: A detective, acting in character, berates a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone seeking a position or honour, a candidate or hopeful.

clue.text: Component of vehicle, one gremlins cut off?

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong, a signal that these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car part gets damaged when mischievous gremlins sever it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of ONE GREMLINS CUT, all fourteen letters; the question mark admits the gremlins are fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: A steering column is the shaft linking a car's steering wheel to its steering gear, a part of the vehicle.

clue.text: Bone covered by skin customarily

indicators.note: the letters are covered by, that is held inside, the words skin customarily

explanation.surface: Bone is normally sheathed in skin, a simple fact of anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' signals the letters inside sKIN CUStomarily.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus, or anvil, is one of the three tiny bones of the middle ear.

clue.text: Designer with substance containing genetic code coming up with robot in human form

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the pieces read from bottom to top, so both are reversed together

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer
DNA is the molecule that carries genetic information

explanation.surface: A fashion designer, together with some genetic material, emerges with a humanoid machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses the designer and the genetic material as one string, so the genetic code ends up in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a machine built to look and behave like a person, a humanoid automaton.

clue.text: In goal, put in effort

indicators.note: one word is put in the other, placed inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt or effort
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football coach says to make an effort at scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but it is the definition, in the sense of fashionable; 'put in' sets the goal word inside the effort word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in is currently in vogue, just as a trendy item is fashionable.

clue.text: Sound conclusion of academic work by person about Thackeray's first book

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: the person word goes about, round the outside of, the other pieces

parts.note: a bod is an informal word for a person

indicators.note: the first letter of the novelist's name is taken

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A scholarly piece written by a critic about Thackeray's debut novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is an adjective here, meaning reliable, not a noise. 'about' wraps the person word round Thackeray's initial and the book word.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper-bottomed means thoroughly reliable, as ships with copper-sheathed hulls were; sound in the sense of solid and trustworthy.

clue.text: Roving sailor after loot sadly caught by enemy

indicators.note: the inner pieces are caught, held fast, by the enemy word around them

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: the sailor comes after the rearranged loot
sadly means badly, a signal that the letters of loot are rearranged

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A wandering seaman is captured by hostile forces after a botched robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges LOOT to OTLO, and 'after' puts the sailor behind it; 'caught by' wraps the enemy word round both. OS, ordinary seaman, is a stock crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Footloose means free to go where one likes, unattached and roaming.

clue.text: Man lacking gallantry to join soldiers in group

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, especially towards women
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An ungentlemanly fellow enlists in a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained people, as of officers or party activists.

clue.text: soup with fish instead of duck

clue.text: Answer from Democrat certainly not, on reflection, embracing society led by Republican

indicators.note: the Republican goes at the head, leading the rest

parts.note: R is the US abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: one piece embraces the other, holding it inside
a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nope is a firm no
D is the US abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A politician answers a Democrat with a flat no, yet the reply turns round to take in a Republican-led group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns NOPE into EPON; 'embracing' puts S inside to give ESPON; R is 'led by', placed first, and D ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, to give an answer.

clue.text: Forward getting a record broken by end of season

indicators.note: the record word is broken open by a letter put inside it

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A striker obtains a record that is broken at the close of the football season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' season gives N; 'broken by' puts it inside LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Along means onward, as in move along, going forward.

clue.text: Information rejected in course of study by English traitor

indicators.note: the rejected piece sits in the course of, in the middle of, the study word

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Intelligence is turned down while studying an Englishman who betrayed his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the information word round; 'in course of' sets it inside the study word. To 'read' a subject is British for studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts his side or cause, a turncoat or traitor.

clue.text: Lack of sophistication shown by cowboy mostly on lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A ranch hand's crude manners are on display at a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks the cowboy's last letter; in a down clue 'on' puts that piece above the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaucherie is social awkwardness or tactlessness, a want of polish and refinement.

clue.text: Representative from Georgia involved in strike

indicators.note: one piece is involved in, wrapped inside, the other

parts.note: to strike out text is to delete it
GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: A union official from the state of Georgia takes part in industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but it means strike out; 'involved in' sets the state abbreviation inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a person sent to act or vote on behalf of others.

clue.text: One in schmooze getting animated, missing hotel of bygone era

indicators.note: getting animated means becoming lively and stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone in a gushing conversation gets excited, ignoring the hotel of an earlier age.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus SCHMOOZE, 'getting animated', with H dropped ('missing hotel'), rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mesozoic is the geological era of the dinosaurs, long past.

clue.text: Scrutinise confession of one who cries in hearing?

indicators.note: in hearing means as it sounds when spoken, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: a weeper admitting it would say 'I bawl'

explanation.surface: Someone asks a tearful person to own up in a courtroom hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The admission 'I bawl', said out loud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is to look at it closely, to examine or stare at it.

clue.text: Prudent to follow accepted practice

indicators.note: the prudent word follows, coming after the other

parts.note: U means upper-class and so socially acceptable
sage means wise or prudent

explanation.surface: It is wise to go along with established custom.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class, socially accepted, usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the habitual way something is done or said.

clue.text: A series of steps to guard against recession? On the contrary

indicators.note: the outer pieces guard the inner one, surrounding it

parts.note: a dance is a sequence of steps
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A routine of steps protects against economic downturn, or rather the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to guard' puts V inside A DANCE. The definition is the opposite of recession, a going back.
explanation.definitionFit: A recession is a moving back; its opposite is moving forward, progress.

clue.text: Arrogant pup, beginning to heckle, is out of order

indicators.note: out of order means jumbled, a signal that the letters are rearranged
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky young dog barking at a speaker is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' heckle gives H; with PUP and IS it is 'out of order', rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppish means self-assertive or haughty, a synonym for arrogant.

clue.text: Attending to show

definitions.meaning: being there, as in all members ...
to put on display or exhibit

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both being in attendance and offering something for view.

clue.text: Number to a large extent upset about new price

indicators.note: the reversed letters go about, round, the new letter
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, reversed
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A figure is largely overturned when the new cost is set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a large extent' cuts SEVEN to SEVE; 'upset' turns it to EVES; 'about' wraps it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, evens is odds of one to one, a price where the stake is matched.

clue.text: Triumphant cry by old monarch entering shelter in port

indicators.note: the inner pieces enter, go inside, the shelter word

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
ha is an exclamation of triumph
VR is Victoria Regina, Queen Victoria

explanation.surface: A shout of victory from a former king as he reaches harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts the cry and Queen Victoria's royal cipher, VR, inside the shelter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major seaport in Normandy, northern France.

clue.text: Grim agent's persona

indicators.note: the apostrophe s stands for has, so the words have the letters within them

explanation.surface: A secret agent's grim public face.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside grIM AGEnt.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is the public impression a person projects, a persona.

clue.text: Excellent lawyer keeping a lot of extra notes

indicators.note: the excellent word keeps, holds inside, the trimmed piece

parts.note: mean is slang for excellent, as in a mean guitar player

indicators.note: a lot of the word, all but its last letter

parts.note: more means extra
DA is a US district attorney, a lawyer

explanation.surface: A top attorney keeps lots of additional jottings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' means mean in its slang sense; 'a lot of' docks the last letter of the extra word, and 'keeping' holds that inside. DA, district attorney, is American.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda is the plural of memorandum, written reminders or notes.

clue.text: Problems filling hole up in sloping ground

indicators.note: one piece fills the other, going inside it

parts.note: to hole up is to hide away
ills are troubles or problems

explanation.surface: Troubles pile into a pit dug on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole up' reads as a hole above, but it is a verb phrase meaning hide; 'filling' puts the problems word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillside is the slope of a hill, ground that slopes.

clue.text: Defeat with no small honour

indicators.note: with no means the letter is taken out

parts.note: a reverse is a setback or defeat

explanation.surface: A loss that comes with no minor honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no small' removes S from REVERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to hold in deep respect, to honour.
